claims.kickoff_quote: Hand the auditor all three of the things it establishes before it can map law to controls, rather than letting it guess them: which regulations actually apply, what categories of personal or regulated data this milestone touches, and which jurisdictions the users and the data sit in.

claims.reasoning: The three enumerated items are a one-to-one re-listing of the agent's own step 1 (applicable regulations / data types / geography), and the KICKOFF text even says these are things 'it establishes' — conceding the agent already owns them. The residual instruction ('supply them rather than let it guess') is a thin wrapper around a list the agent's first numbered step already fixes; only the scoping word 'this milestone' is operator-supplied.

claims.kickoff_quote: Point it at any prior audit history and existing control or policy docs too.

The KICKOFF sentence re-derives a handoff both files already enforce; only the trigger predicate is arguably operator judgement.

claims.kickoff_quote: Disclosure deadlines start running from discovery, not from the fix, so surface the applicable regime and its clock to me while the incident is still open.
claims.skill_quote: SEARCH EVIDENCE — closest sentence in the asset is the Output section, line 25: 'An audit report: executive summary, per-control findings with evidence, a risk matrix, and a prioritized remediation roadmap. State control-coverage percentage and any critical findings.' The asset's only other mention of deadlines is line 17 ('breach-notification deadlines') as a topic area. Greps run over compliance-auditor.md (no references/ dir exists — confirmed by ls of plugins/dev-kit-core/agents/): -niE 'deadline|clock|early|interim|urgent|immediat|discovery|72|notif' returned only lines 17 and 25. Nothing in the asset requires an interim, pre-report output, and nothing anchors the clock to discovery rather than remediation.
claims.reasoning: The asset's only specified deliverable is a full audit report; it never mandates surfacing the applicable regime and its notification clock as an early interim output while an incident is live, and never states that the clock starts at discovery. incident-responder.md:24 covers 'track disclosure deadlines' generically but not the discovery-anchored rule. So this KICKOFF sentence is load-bearing and must be KEPT — the finding is that compliance-auditor.md should carry it.

consistency: The two invocations are compatible in substance but asymmetric in dispatch shape: step 12 says the agent needs a paired product-lane skill (gdpr-ccpa-compliance / hipaa-compliance) 'for framework detail', while step 15 asks the same agent alone for 'the framework-specific breach-notification obligations' with no companion skill. If the framework detail genuinely lives in the product-lane skills, the step-15 handoff is under-equipped; if the agent can supply it alone (compliance-auditor.md:16-17 suggests it can), the step-12 pairing is the questionable half. Low severity, but the guide should pick one story.
